Apple must respond by Monday to a complaint Epic Games has filed with Brazil's antitrust regulator, accusing Apple of imposing restrictive interpretations of its obligations under a recent antitrust settlement regarding the Brazilian App Store. Details below.

Background

Two months ago, Apple announced that developers could now distribute apps through alternative app marketplaces in Brazil.

The change was part of a settlement that ended a years-long antitrust investigation triggered by a complaint from Latin American e-commerce giant MercadoLibre over Apple's App Store rules.

Under the new terms, Brazilian developers can distribute iOS apps through alternative marketplaces and offer payment methods outside of Apple's IAP system.

Apple also introduced a new commission structure, including a 5% Core Technology Fee on sales of digital goods and services made inside apps distributed outside the App Store. More details on the structure can be found here.

Epic challenges Apple's implementation

According to a report by Brazil's O Globo today, citing MacMagazine, Epic recently submitted a petition to Brazilian antitrust regulator CADE accusing Apple of establishing "structural, technical, and access barriers" that undermine the practical viability of alternative app distribution.

Epic says that while the new Brazilian terms apply only to iOS apps, Apple's agreement with CADE "explicitly covers iPadOS."

Epic is also reportedly objecting to what it describes as "scare screen pop-ups," arguing they deter users from installing apps from outside the App Store. It also criticized the current installation flow, saying it requires nine steps—three more than Apple's current setup in Europe.

O Globo reports that Epic added that Apple's original installation flow in Europe required 15 steps, but after being forced to reduce it to 6, the "download abandonment rate dropped from 65% to 25%."

Finally, Epic told CADE that Apple's reporting requirements "go well beyond what is needed to compute charges," allowing it to "monitor competitors' business models."

O Globo reports that CADE gave Apple until Monday to submit a response. Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
